newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank chief reviews India reforms with RBI.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief reviews India reforms with RBI.

text.p: The World Bank on Monday reviewed the progress of India's economic reforms with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), its president James Wolfensohn said.

Wolfensohn, who met the RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan in the morning, told a news conference he would reserve comments on the reforms until he discussed them with officials of the federal government in New Delhi later this week.
"Maharashtra's performance (in utilising World Bank aid) has been very good," he said, referring to India's richest province.
He said the bank agreed to have regular reviews on project implementation with the state chief minister.
Wolfensohn listed Maharashtra's problems as its 5.5 million slum population, water, infrastructure and the AIDS threat.

The World Bank president said he visited Bombay's busy Churchgate suburban rail terminus on Monday morning, adding that the bank would help in relocating people who would be displaced in a track widening programme on Bombay's suburban railways.
Wolfensohn and a World Bank team, on the first leg of their India tour, leaves for the southern city of Bangalore later on Monday.
